since it is composed of ἐς and τε (as rightly Etym. M. p. 382, 7), as ὥστε from ὡς and τε, I have written separately ἔς τε, to distinguish it from the verb ἐστέ, just as we write the pronoun ὅτι separately, to distinguish it from the particle ὅτι. In manuscripts of other writers sometimes ἕστε is written with a rough breathing, according to the opinion of certain grammarians (see Eustath. p. 162, 42), who thought it arose from ἕως τε. until.
Thus Stanley for εἰτ᾽ ἀφίκετο [then he came].
